summary: workflow status's --json/--agent output builds a structured envelope ({store_status, resources: {<name>: {count, last_synced_at?}}, total, store_path, next_step when empty}) instead of json-encoding a bare Status() map. store.LastSyncedTimes() unions sync_state (flat resources) with resources.synced_at MAX per type, since parent-keyed dependents (performance, workout_details) only get a sync_state row under --full mode's compound-key backfill tracking, not in the default sync path. store.HasSyncHistory() (any sync_state row at all) gates the "empty" classification, since Status()'s row counts alone can't tell "never synced" apart from "synced with zero results." A regen touching this command must preserve both fallbacks and the empty-store shape (matching the "search" MCP tool's).
reason: workflow_status(json=true)/workflow_status(agent=true) returned a bare {} on an empty store while plain-text mode gave a real message -- the modes agents actually use had nothing actionable. Review also found the first version of this fix omitted dependent-resource timestamps and could misreport a real zero-result sync as never having run.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. Tests cover the empty-store envelope shape, a real archive's flat (workouts) and dependent (performance) resource timestamps, and that a completed zero-result sync reports store_status "ready" rather than "empty".
